correctness.rationale: At time \(t=w\), Hamming distance forces every contributing path to be a permutation of the target support. The uniform initial coin is fixed by the Grover diffusion; every later shortest-path transition is off-diagonal with amplitude \(2/n\). Counting \((w-1)!\) coherent paths per final coin sector and \(w\) orthogonal sectors gives the exact probability. The classical count and Stirling limit then follow directly. Exact finite-state replay independently matches every \(2\le n\le7\), \(1\le w\le n\) case.

originality.rationale: The originality-bearing statement is the exact all-Hamming-weight earliest-arrival profile and its quantum/classical exponential crossover at \(\rho=e/4\). The motivating dispersion paper gives the walk, shell recurrences, and a factorial inequality but not this equality or crossover. Kempe gives an opposite-corner spectral amplitude and later near-unit hitting window, not the full earliest-arrival frontier. Moore--Russell gives mixing results, not this boundary law. Targeted semantic and exact-form searches found no indexed statement covering the profile or crossover.
residual_risks: A weakly indexed derivation of the same shortest-time factorial profile may exist under path-counting or radial-walk terminology.

Kempe's opposite-corner spectral formula is broad enough to recover the antipodal specialization after further calculation; originality therefore rests on the all-Hamming-weight frontier and the \(e/4\) quantum/classical crossover, not on the antipodal line by itself.

value.rationale: The causal boundary \(t=d(0,x)\) is a natural dynamical regime, not an arbitrary time slice. The result gives the entire point-probability profile there and identifies a sharp normalized-distance threshold \(e/4\) where coherent shortest-path interference changes from exponential suppression to exponential amplification relative to the simple classical walk. This complements later-time dispersion and antipodal-hitting results by exposing a structural boundary mechanism.
